questions.question: In which city was Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart born in 1756?
questions.hint: The city was then a small state ruled by a prince-archbishop, and Mozart's father played the violin in his orchestra. A chocolate sweet named after the composer comes from there.
questions.explanation: Mozart was born on 27 January 1756 in a house in the Getreidegasse, which is now a museum. Salzburg became part of Austria for good only in 1816. In 1781 he quarrelled with the archbishop, left his service and settled in Vienna, where he lived for the rest of his life.

image.alt: A painting: a young man and a young woman sit side by side at a keyboard; an older man holds a violin, and a woman's portrait hangs on the wall.

questions.question: Beethoven's Ninth Symphony ends with a choir singing a poem by Friedrich Schiller. What is the poem called?
questions.hint: Schiller wrote it in 1785. Beethoven's tune for it has been the anthem of the European Union since 1985.
questions.explanation: The Ninth was first played in Vienna on 7 May 1824. It was the first symphony by a major composer to use singers. In the poem, Schiller dreams of a world in which all people become brothers.

questions.question: The Toccata and Fugue in D minor is one of the best-known pieces that carry Bach's name. For which instrument is it written?
questions.hint: Bach was an expert on them: towns asked him to come and judge new ones when they were built. At 18 he got his first post as a player of one, in the town of Arnstadt.
questions.explanation: In his lifetime Bach was known above all as an organist. The piece became world famous when Walt Disney's film Fantasia opened with it in 1940, played by a full orchestra. Some scholars doubt that Bach wrote it, because its style is unusual for him. No copy in his own hand survives.

questions.question: Mozart was still writing his last work when he died in Vienna in December 1791. What kind of work is it?
questions.hint: A stranger ordered it in secret for a count, who wanted to pass it off as his own work. Mozart's pupil Süssmayr completed it.
questions.explanation: Mozart died on 5 December 1791, aged 35, and left the Requiem unfinished. The count wanted it in memory of his wife, and Mozart's widow Constanze had it completed in secret so that she could be paid for it. There is no evidence for the old story that the composer Salieri poisoned him.

questions.question: Which of Beethoven's symphonies opens with four famous notes, three short and one long?
questions.hint: It is in C minor. It was first played in Vienna in December 1808, at a concert that lasted four hours in a freezing cold theatre.
questions.explanation: The four notes come back again and again through the whole symphony. In the Second World War the BBC used them as a signal to occupied Europe: in Morse code, three dots and a dash are the letter V, for victory. The story that Beethoven called them "fate knocking at the door" comes from his secretary Schindler, who is not a reliable witness.

questions.question: In which city did Bach work for the last 27 years of his life, as director of music at St Thomas's Church?
questions.hint: He arrived in 1723 and taught the boys of the church's choir school. He wrote the St Matthew Passion and most of his cantatas there.
questions.explanation: Bach was cantor of St Thomas's in Leipzig from 1723 until his death in 1750. In his first years there he wrote a new cantata for the city's churches almost every week. His grave has been in the church since 1950.

questions.question: Which opera by Mozart, first performed in Prague in 1787, has a stone statue come to supper and drag the hero down to hell?
questions.hint: The words are by the Italian poet Lorenzo Da Ponte. The hero is a Spanish nobleman, and his servant Leporello keeps a list of the women he has seduced.
questions.explanation: Don Giovanni is the old Spanish story of Don Juan. He kills the father of a woman he has tried to seduce, and later he mockingly invites the dead man's statue to supper. Da Ponte also wrote the words of The Marriage of Figaro and Così fan tutte.

questions.question: In 1802 Beethoven wrote a long, despairing letter to his brothers and never sent it. It is known as the Heiligenstadt Testament. What is it about?
options: His love for a married woman
questions.hint: He was 31 and had kept the trouble secret for years. The letter was found among his papers after his death in 1827.
questions.explanation: Beethoven's hearing began to fail in his twenties. In the letter he says that he had thought of ending his life, and that only his art held him back. He went on composing for almost 25 more years. At the first performance of his Ninth Symphony, it is said, a singer had to turn him round so that he could see the audience clapping.

questions.question: After Bach's death his St Matthew Passion was almost forgotten. Which composer conducted it in Berlin in 1829 and so began the great revival of Bach's music?
questions.hint: He was only 20 years old. He later wrote the Wedding March and a famous violin concerto.
questions.explanation: Mendelssohn conducted the Passion at the Berlin Sing-Akademie on 11 March 1829, about a hundred years after Bach wrote it. The hall was full, and the concert had to be repeated. From then on Bach was seen as one of the greatest of all composers.

questions.question: Mozart wrote his last symphony, No. 41 in C major, in the summer of 1788. By which name is it known?
questions.hint: The name is not Mozart's. It was given after his death, probably by a concert manager in London.
questions.explanation: Mozart wrote his last three symphonies in about two months in the summer of 1788. The name "Jupiter", after the king of the Roman gods, probably came from the London concert manager Johann Peter Salomon. The "Haffner", the "Linz" and the "Prague" are earlier symphonies by Mozart.

image.alt: A portrait of a man in a white wig and a red coat with gold trim.

label.title: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (painted after his death)
